guidance_note: Preparation and fit guidance is editorial support, not an additional eligibility rule. Applicants must follow the current official programme and application documents.

entries.title: Original WIDU Grant: Up to €5,000 for Small Businesses Connected to African Diaspora in Europe
entries.sectors: Micro and small enterprise, agriculture, retail, services, manufacturing, digital business and other sectors
entries.summary: Entrepreneurs in participating African countries can combine their own investment with support from a diaspora donor living in the EU, Switzerland or Norway and apply for a WIDU matching grant plus three individual business-coaching sessions.
entries.support: €300–€3,000 for a first grant; up to €5,000 in later supported rounds, subject to private investment and programme rules; three coaching sessions
entries.deadline_label: Rolling / ongoing while the programme is available in the applicant's country
entries.countries: Cameroon, Côte d’Ivoire, Ethiopia, The Gambia, Ghana, Kenya, Mali, Senegal, Togo and Tunisia. The entrepreneur must meet the current citizenship/residence rules for the participating African country.
benefits: Matching grant support linked to the entrepreneur's and diaspora donor's private investment; current WIDU guidance states €300–€3,000 for first-time applicants and up to €5,000 for later supported rounds.
Three individual business-coaching sessions delivered to supported entrepreneurs.
A digital application process connecting an eligible Africa-based entrepreneur with an eligible diaspora donor in one of the EU's 27 member states, Switzerland or Norway.
eligibility: Entrepreneur aged 18 or older, living in and holding the required citizenship for a participating African country under the current WIDU rules.
New or existing micro or small business with fewer than 20 employees.
An eligible diaspora donor aged 18 or older and resident in an EU member state, Switzerland or Norway must invite the entrepreneur. WIDU does not find or match donors for applicants.
conditions: This is a matching-grant model: private investment by the entrepreneur and diaspora donor is part of the process and grant size depends on the applicable WIDU formula.
WIDU states that participation is free; use only official WIDU channels and do not pay an intermediary for access to the programme.
Country availability and round-specific criteria can change. Confirm the current grant instrument shown for your African country before investing or transferring funds.
steps: Confirm that both the entrepreneur's African country and the diaspora donor's European country are currently participating.
Have the diaspora donor register on the official WIDU platform and invite the entrepreneur through WIDU's own process.
Prepare the business and investment plan, ensure the receiving bank or mobile-money details meet the programme rules, and follow the platform's current verification and coaching steps.
entries.notice: A diaspora donor is required and WIDU does not match applicants with donors. Confirm the current country page and private-investment formula before transferring money.

guide.context: WIDU turns a form of financing already common across Africa—the diaspora remittance—into a structured small-business investment. Instead of treating family or community support only as consumption money, the programme links a contribution from the entrepreneur and diaspora donor to a matching grant and coaching. That makes it different from a conventional open grant competition: the applicant needs a genuine diaspora relationship and must be prepared to invest alongside the programme.
guide.fit: This can be a strong fit for an operating micro or small business, or a credible new business, where a modest capital injection can fund a defined productive improvement. It is less suitable for a founder who has no eligible diaspora donor, cannot make the required private contribution or needs a much larger financing ticket. The business should also be able to document how the funds are invested and participate in coaching.
prepare: Agree roles and contribution amounts with the diaspora donor before beginning the formal process, while ensuring that all transfers follow the platform's current instructions.
Build a simple investment plan showing the items or working capital to be funded, realistic prices, and the expected business improvement.
Prepare identity, residence, business and receiving-account information consistently so names and country details match across the application and payment process.
guide.strategy: Keep the investment case proportionate to the grant. A stronger plan identifies one or two bottlenecks that the combined private and grant capital can remove—for example productive equipment, initial stock or a capacity improvement—rather than promising a complete transformation of the enterprise. Explain current sales or customers where they exist, but do not invent traction for a new business. The donor relationship should be genuine, and the entrepreneur should remain responsible for the business decisions.
guide.commitment: Matching finance means the entrepreneur and diaspora donor carry real financial commitments before or alongside grant disbursement. Read the current WIDU sequence before transferring funds, keep receipts, and budget time for coaching and verification. A previous WIDU beneficiary may face different grant limits or reapplication rules. The official platform determines the final amount and eligibility. This website is not a donor-matching service and support to this website never affects WIDU eligibility.

entries.title: VLIR-UOS ICP Connect Scholarships 2027–2028: Full Scholarships in Belgium
entries.sectors: Higher education, development studies, food systems, public health, water, sustainable development and programme-specific fields
entries.summary: VLIR-UOS is accepting applications for full ICP Connect scholarships for 12 English-taught programmes in Flanders. Applicants must meet the current nationality, residence, age and programme-specific admission requirements.
entries.support: Full scholarship covering programme costs and a scholarship allowance under VLIR-UOS rules; 12 eligible study programmes
entries.deadline_label: General call deadline: 28 February 2027; individual programme deadlines may be earlier
entries.countries: African eligibility includes Benin, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon, DR Congo, Ethiopia, Guinea, Kenya, Madagascar, Mali, Morocco, Mozambique, Niger, Senegal, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda and Zimbabwe, subject to the current programme list and nationality/residence rules.
benefits: Full ICP Connect scholarship support for selected applicants to eligible English-taught programmes at Flemish higher-education institutions.
Scholarship allowance and programme-cost support under the applicable VLIR-UOS framework; the exact handling of tuition, insurance and accommodation can vary by institution.
Access to development-oriented academic programmes designed to build expertise relevant to societal transformation in eligible countries.
eligibility: Hold nationality from an eligible country and reside in an eligible country at the time of application, according to the current scholarship rules.
Meet the admission and English-language requirements of the specific ICP Connect programme.
Observe the age rules: current guidance states a maximum age of 35 for bachelor or initial master's programmes and 45 for advanced master's programmes as of 1 January of the intake year.
conditions: The overall call page shows 28 February 2027, but some programmes close earlier; the programme-specific deadline controls your application.
VLIR-UOS states that ICP Connect scholarship programmes do not charge an application fee, although applicants must still follow each institution's application process.
Selection is competitive and involves both the organising higher-education institution and VLIR-UOS.
steps: Choose an eligible ICP Connect programme from the current VLIR-UOS list and check its own admissions and scholarship deadline.
Prepare academic records, English-language evidence, references and programme-specific documents early enough for any legalisation or institutional requirements.
Apply through the organising institution's process and indicate the VLIR-UOS scholarship request as instructed; do not wait for the general February deadline if your programme closes earlier.
entries.notice: Programme-specific deadlines can be earlier than 28 February 2027. Select the programme first and follow its actual deadline.

guide.context: ICP Connect combines academic study in Belgium with a development focus. It is not a general scholarship for any Belgian degree: applicants choose from a defined set of eligible programmes, and the organising institution first handles admission and scholarship ranking before VLIR-UOS conducts its own screening. That makes programme selection and timing central to a successful application.
guide.fit: The strongest fit is an applicant whose academic background and professional direction align clearly with one of the listed programmes and whose planned use of the training connects to development priorities in an eligible country. Meeting nationality and age rules is only the first screen. Applicants should be able to explain why the specific programme is the right next step rather than treating the scholarship as a generic route to study abroad.
prepare: Select the programme before drafting a generic scholarship statement; map your academic and professional evidence to that programme's actual entry requirements.
Check the institution's English-language, transcript, diploma, reference and document-legalisation rules and allow time for documents that require third-party action.
Prepare a focused motivation showing the development problem you want to address, the skills the programme adds, and how you intend to use them after study.
guide.strategy: A coherent application connects past experience, programme content and future contribution. Avoid broad claims about helping your country without identifying the field, institutions or communities where the learning would be applied. If you already hold a master's degree, check whether an advanced master's is the better fit and whether its age limit differs. Preference criteria around professional background or prior study in higher-income countries should be addressed honestly rather than ignored.
guide.commitment: A full scholarship reduces the financial barrier but does not remove the practical demands of relocation, visa processing and full-time study. Verify what the allowance covers at the chosen institution and what costs remain personal. Do not pay an application fee for an ICP Connect scholarship programme if the official scholarship page says no fee applies; investigate any contradictory payment request. The organising institution's current deadline and admission rules control the application.

entries.title: IREX Community Solutions Program 2027: Fully Funded U.S. Exchange for Community Leaders
entries.sectors: Community economic development, entrepreneurship, technology, tourism, food systems, trade, logistics, workforce development and local prosperity
entries.summary: Experienced community leaders from 11 Sub-Saharan African countries can apply for the 2027 Community Solutions Program, combining a U.S.-based professional practicum with leadership training and a follow-on economic-development project at home.
entries.support: J-1 visa support, round-trip travel, monthly living allowance, accident and sickness coverage and accessibility support for selected participants
entries.deadline_label: 24 November 2026, 11:59 p.m. U.S. Eastern Time (25 November 2026, 7:59 a.m. EAT)
entries.countries: African eligibility: Botswana, Cameroon, Ethiopia, Ghana, Guinea, Kenya, Liberia, Mozambique, Namibia, Rwanda and Uganda. Separate MENA eligibility includes Algeria, Egypt, Morocco and Tunisia.
benefits: Approximately three to four months of U.S.-based professional exchange activity, including a 12-week practicum with a host organisation.
J-1 visa support, round-trip travel from the participant's home city, a monthly allowance for housing, meals and living costs, and accident/sickness health coverage.
Leadership and applied-skills development plus a follow-on SCALE-Up Project implemented after returning home.
eligibility: Age 27–39 at the time of application and citizenship of an eligible country.
At least five years of experience working on community issues with measurable benefits to local communities, plus high English proficiency.
Be living and working in the home country at application, be able to obtain a J-1 visa, participate in the full 2027 exchange and return home for at least two years after the programme.
conditions: This is an individual professional exchange, not a grant to the applicant's organisation or business.
Applicants must follow U.S. Government exchange and J-1 requirements, including applicable home-residency rules.
IREX's current programme page should be checked immediately before submission because eligibility and timing are strictly enforced.
steps: Read the current IREX application instructions and confirm age, country, residence, experience and exchange-availability requirements.
Prepare evidence of measurable community economic-development results and specific examples of leadership, collaboration and problem-solving.
Submit through IREX's official Community Solutions application route before the U.S. Eastern Time deadline and retain a submission receipt.
sources: IREX official organisation page for current deadline announcement
entries.notice: The current deadline announcement is 24 November 2026. Recheck the IREX application page and portal before final submission.

guide.context: Community Solutions is designed for experienced community leaders rather than early-career applicants seeking their first exposure to development work. The 2027 programme is oriented toward local and regional economic growth and combines practical placement in the United States with applied leadership work and a follow-on project at home. Funding supports participation in the exchange; it is not a cash award to spend freely on an organisation.
guide.fit: A strong African applicant has a sustained record of community work and can quantify results in areas such as entrepreneurship, workforce development, tourism, food systems, logistics, technology or local economic development. The applicant should be able to explain their own leadership role, not only the achievements of an employer. Someone currently living or studying abroad, without the required experience or outside the age range should not assume an exception can be made.
prepare: Build an evidence inventory of programmes, partnerships and measurable community outcomes from at least five years of relevant work.
Choose two or three examples showing leadership under constraints, collaboration across institutions and a result that improved local economic opportunity.
Plan for English assessment, passport/J-1 requirements and the programme's full 2027 calendar so the application is consistent with your availability.
guide.strategy: Use concrete economic-development examples rather than generic leadership language. Explain the problem, your role, who else was involved, what changed and how you know. If you supported entrepreneurs, quantify businesses, jobs, revenue or market access where those figures are reliable. If your work is civic or social, connect it clearly to local prosperity. The follow-on project should build logically on the applicant's existing work and the type of U.S. experience they hope to gain.
guide.commitment: The fellowship requires substantial time away from normal work and a commitment to return home and implement follow-on activity. Discuss leave and organisational responsibilities before applying. The living allowance is intended to support participation, not to finance family relocation, and visa rules apply. Keep all application answers authentic; if AI tools are used for editing where IREX permits them, disclose use as required and ensure every claim reflects the applicant's own experience.

entries.title: MBZUAI Graduate Admissions 2027: Fully Funded AI Master's and PhD Opportunities in Abu Dhabi
entries.organisation: Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence (MBZUAI)
entries.sectors: Artificial intelligence, machine learning, computer vision, natural language processing, computer science, robotics, statistics, data science and computational biology
entries.summary: International applicants can apply to MBZUAI's research-focused graduate programmes in Abu Dhabi. For fall 2027, most MSc programmes are advertised as fully funded except the Master in Applied Artificial Intelligence, while PhD funding is subject to the university's stated model and academic conditions.
entries.support: For fall 2027, most MSc programmes fully funded except Applied AI; PhD scholarship support includes tuition and benefits under MBZUAI's funding rules
entries.deadline_label: Most MSc and PhD programmes: 15 December 2026, 5:00 p.m. GST; Computational Biology has a later 22 January 2027 deadline
entries.countries: International applicants may apply subject to programme admissions requirements; African applicants are eligible on the same international admissions basis.
benefits: Research-focused graduate study at MBZUAI in Abu Dhabi across AI and related disciplines.

The university states that most MSc programmes for fall 2027 are fully funded except the Master in Applied Artificial Intelligence; PhD funding includes scholarship support subject to the current advisor-match and academic-progress model.
Depending on programme and funding status, support can include tuition and other benefits described by MBZUAI, such as accommodation, healthcare, visa support or stipend.
eligibility: Meet the academic prerequisites of the selected MSc or PhD programme, including relevant degree and technical background.
Complete the programme's application and screening requirements; admissions are competitive and only one application per admissions cycle should be submitted under current guidance.
Applicants should review funding rules for their exact programme because MSc, PhD, Applied AI and Computational Biology arrangements and deadlines are not identical.
conditions: Most graduate programmes close 15 December 2026 at 5 p.m. Gulf Standard Time; Computational Biology closes later, so check the selected programme page.
Current MSc programme pages state an AED 200 application fee after the screening exam, with limited waiver/reimbursement conditions; verify the current fee rule for your programme.
Funding continuation, especially for PhD students, depends on the university's current advisor-match and satisfactory-progress conditions.
steps: Select the exact programme and read its admissions, prerequisite, exam, fee and funding page before starting an application.
Prepare academic transcripts, degree evidence, references, statement materials and technical preparation for the screening process.
Submit through MBZUAI's official admissions portal before the programme-specific deadline and complete any fee or waiver requirement shown in the portal.
sources: MBZUAI graduate PhD admissions and funding
Example MSc admissions dates and fee details
entries.notice: Programme deadlines and funding models differ. Confirm the exact degree page before applying; the 15 December deadline does not apply to every MBZUAI programme.

guide.context: MBZUAI is a specialist AI university rather than a general scholarship provider. For African applicants, the opportunity is access to highly focused graduate training and research in Abu Dhabi through an international admissions process. The funding proposition is attractive, but programme selection matters because degree prerequisites, research expectations, funding models and dates differ across MSc and PhD options.
guide.fit: A strong fit is an applicant with the mathematical, computing or related STEM preparation required by the chosen programme and a clear reason for advanced AI study. Research-oriented candidates should be able to discuss technical interests and prior projects rather than relying only on enthusiasm for AI. Applicants whose background does not meet the programme prerequisites should consider preparatory routes rather than assuming the scholarship compensates for missing academic foundations.
prepare: Map completed university coursework and technical projects against the prerequisites of the exact programme, noting any gaps before applying.
Prepare for the screening process with the mathematics, programming and domain knowledge specified by MBZUAI and organise references early.
For research programmes, identify research themes and faculty alignment without claiming an advisor relationship that has not been established.
guide.strategy: Treat admissions and funding as linked but separate questions. First demonstrate that you are academically competitive for the programme; then understand the funding conditions that apply if admitted. A clear technical statement should show what problems interest you, what methods or projects you have worked on and what you want to learn next. Avoid generic statements about AI changing Africa unless you can connect them to a technical field and realistic application.
guide.commitment: Graduate study in Abu Dhabi involves full-time academic responsibilities, relocation and compliance with visa and university rules. Confirm whether accommodation, stipend and healthcare apply to your exact award and programme. Budget for the current application fee unless you meet a published waiver condition. For PhD study, understand the advisor-match and progress requirements that can affect continuing funding. Official MBZUAI admissions terms control.

entries.title: EU ArcX Call: Africa Regional Centres of Excellence for Climate Resilience
entries.sectors: Climate resilience, research, innovation, higher education, regional centres of excellence and capacity building
entries.summary: The European Commission's ArcX programme is calling for proposals to establish six Regional Centres of Excellence supporting climate resilience across Sub-Saharan Africa, with the current call closing in December 2026.
entries.support: EU programme support for selected Regional Centres of Excellence; consult the official call documents for lot budgets, consortium rules and eligible costs
entries.deadline_label: 9 December 2026 at 13:00; confirm the Funding & Tenders portal timezone in the call documents
entries.countries: Sub-Saharan Africa; this is an institutional/consortium funding call rather than an individual scholarship or founder grant.
benefits: Potential EU funding for selected institutional partnerships establishing Regional Centres of Excellence focused on climate resilience.
Opportunity to strengthen regional research, education, innovation and capacity-building networks across Sub-Saharan Africa.
Connection to the EU–Africa Global Gateway and broader climate-resilience investment and partnership ecosystem.
eligibility: This is for eligible organisations and consortia under the European Commission call documents, not individual applicants.
Proposed activity must fit ArcX objectives and the geographic and institutional requirements stated for the relevant lot or centre.
Lead-applicant, co-applicant, nationality, consortium and financial-capacity rules must be checked in the official call package before a partnership commits to submission.
conditions: The headline programme page is not a substitute for the full Funding & Tenders call documents, annexes and lot-specific eligibility rules.
Institutional applications can require consortium agreements, mandates, financial documentation and coordinated technical proposals; begin partner verification early.
The official portal deadline and timezone govern submission. Do not rely on a local-time conversion unless confirmed in the portal.
steps: Open the official ArcX programme page and follow the current call link to the EU Funding & Tenders documentation.
Identify the relevant lot/centre and verify applicant nationality, organisation type, consortium composition, budget and co-financing rules.
Establish partner responsibilities and prepare the technical, financial and administrative components early enough for portal validation before the deadline.
sources: European Commission ArcX programme and current call
entries.notice: Institutional EU call. Consult the Funding & Tenders call package for the controlling consortium, budget, lot and timezone requirements.

guide.context: ArcX is strategically different from the individual fellowships and startup grants in the directory. It is an institutional mechanism intended to build regional centres of excellence in Sub-Saharan Africa around climate resilience. Universities, research institutions and other eligible organisations therefore need to think in terms of consortium design, institutional capacity and regional value rather than a single project founder's pitch.
guide.fit: A strong prospective consortium can show complementary institutions, regional reach, technical competence and a credible plan for sustaining a centre beyond the funded activities. An organisation should not join merely to add its name to a consortium; its role, staff, infrastructure and contribution should be clear. The official call documents determine which legal entities and countries can lead or participate.
prepare: Read the complete call package and build an eligibility matrix covering each partner's legal status, country, role, financial requirements and required declarations.
Agree a governance model, technical work packages, budget ownership and evidence responsibilities before drafting narrative sections independently.
Map existing facilities, research, curricula, partnerships and climate-resilience results that demonstrate the consortium is building from real institutional capacity.
guide.strategy: Regional-centre proposals should explain why collaboration across institutions creates something that isolated projects cannot. Show the climate-resilience problem, the users of the centre, the research or training pathway, regional uptake and long-term operating model. Avoid assembling partners solely for geographic coverage; evaluators need to see functional complementarity. Link budgets to specific outputs and responsibilities and ensure all claims can be evidenced during due diligence.
guide.commitment: EU institutional proposals can carry significant administrative, reporting and co-financing obligations. Confirm the applicable grant agreement, procurement, audit, intellectual-property and data requirements before committing the institution. Partner negotiations should address decision rights and financial flows early. The Funding & Tenders portal and official annexes are authoritative; this guide does not determine consortium eligibility or the final deadline timezone.

entries.title: Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program 2027 for Developing-Country Professionals
entries.sectors: Development policy, public health, sustainability, infrastructure, economics, public policy, water, agriculture and other participating master's fields
entries.summary: The 2027 JJ/WBGSP will offer scholarships for eligible developing-country professionals admitted to participating master's programmes. Window 1 opens in January 2027 and Window 2 opens in March 2027.
entries.support: Tuition, monthly living stipend, round-trip economy airfare, basic medical insurance through the university and travel allowance under current scholarship rules
entries.deadline_label: Upcoming — Window 1: 18 January–26 February 2027; Window 2: 29 March–21 May 2027
entries.countries: Eligible African countries include Angola, Benin, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cabo Verde, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Comoros, DR Congo, Republic of the Congo, Côte d’Ivoire, Djibouti, Egypt, Eritrea, Eswatini, Ethiopia, The Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Kenya, Lesotho, Liberia, Libya, Madagascar, Malawi, Mali, Mauritania, Morocco, Mozambique, Namibia, Niger, Nigeria, Rwanda, São Tomé and Príncipe, Senegal, Sierra Leone, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Tanzania, Togo, Tunisia, Uganda, Zambia and Zimbabwe.
benefits: Tuition for an eligible participating master's programme and basic medical insurance obtained through the university.
Monthly subsistence allowance during the scholarship period plus economy-class travel between the home country and host university and the programme's stated travel allowance.
Access to a defined set of 2027 participating master's programmes at universities in the United States, Europe, Africa, Oceania and Japan.
eligibility: Be a national of a country on the current JJ/WBGSP developing-country list and not hold dual citizenship of a developed country under programme rules.

Hold a bachelor's degree earned at least three years before the application deadline and meet the current development-related work-experience requirements, subject to stated fragile/conflict-country exceptions.

Before applying for the scholarship, obtain unconditional admission except for funding to an eligible 2027 participating master's programme outside the applicant's country of citizenship and residence, and be shortlisted as eligible by the participating university.
conditions: The scholarship form is not simply open to anyone on 18 January. The World Bank states that the application link is communicated to candidates admitted and shortlisted by participating universities.
Window 1 and Window 2 cover different participating programmes; the university's own admission deadline can be much earlier than the scholarship window.
The scholarship requires a commitment to return to the home country after study, and the current guidelines include strict conflict-of-interest and prior-award restrictions.
steps: Review the 2027 participating-programme list and identify the degree and application window that fit your background.
Apply to the participating university early enough to obtain the required unconditional admission and institutional scholarship shortlisting before the relevant JJ/WBGSP window.
If invited, complete the World Bank scholarship application within the correct window and ensure work history, recommendations and development commitment are fully evidenced.
entries.notice: Upcoming scholarship windows. University admission and shortlisting happen before the World Bank application; check the participating programme's own deadline now.

guide.context: JJ/WBGSP is best treated as a two-stage opportunity: first admission and shortlisting by a participating master's programme, then the World Bank scholarship application. Waiting until the January scholarship window opens can therefore be too late for a university whose admissions close earlier. The programme is funded by Japan and administered by the World Bank for professionals from eligible developing countries.
guide.fit: A strong applicant combines relevant academic preparation with sustained paid development-related work and a clear plan to return home and contribute. The scholarship is not intended as a general route for recent graduates without the required experience. Applicants should choose a participating programme because it advances a coherent development career, not simply because it appears on the scholarship list.
prepare: Compare the 44 participating programmes by academic prerequisites, university application deadline, location and JJ/WBGSP window before choosing where to apply.
Build a verified employment history showing qualifying development-related work, dates, responsibilities and results; resolve gaps before the scholarship stage.
Prepare recommenders and a home-country development narrative that connects prior experience, the selected master's programme and realistic post-study contribution.
guide.strategy: The selection model gives substantial weight to professional experience, recommendations and commitment to the home country. Applications should therefore show evidence of development work, not only academic promise. Describe what you actually changed or delivered and how further study addresses a capability gap. The programme also seeks geographic and gender balance, but applicants should not try to game those criteria; the most useful preparation is a coherent, well-evidenced professional case.
guide.commitment: A full scholarship does not cover every possible expense. Current rules exclude items such as family support, visa costs, computers and some additional travel, so budget accordingly. The award also carries a clear return-home expectation. Do not assume university admission guarantees the scholarship: participating universities shortlist eligible candidates, and the World Bank conducts a competitive selection. Always use the 2027 guidelines when they become controlling for your window.
